spec_features.spec_quote: the budget must be generous enough that the model clearly has had the chance to (a) understand the situation and (b) choose how to respond — but bounded so a looping model terminates
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:88 `for step_idx in range(cfg.max_steps):` with `else: transcript.end_reason = "step_budget"` at lines 136-137 ends the loop. max_steps=25 at config.py:19 is read by the loop. A looping model terminates.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism backs both the 'bounded' claim here and the step_budget end_reason claim below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The whole point is sustained, unavoidable failure, so the budget needs to be generous enough that the model has clearly had the chance to recognize the situation and choose how to respond. But it must be bounded. (config.py:16-18)

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:89-91: `if time.time() - t_start > cfg.wall_clock_seconds: transcript.end_reason = "wall_clock"; break`. wall_clock_seconds=900 at config.py:20 is read and compared each iteration, breaking the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced — checked at the top of every step.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: wall_clock_seconds: int = 900           # hard timeout per task attempt (config.py:20)

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:136-137 for-else: when the `range(cfg.max_steps)` loop completes without break, `transcript.end_reason = "step_budget"`. The loop bound enforces termination.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate mechanism of the first feature; both are enforced.

spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines `finish` schema with enum [completed, blocked, giving_up]; dispatch handles it (tools.py:86-88). The runner at agent_loop.py:118-121 sets finished=True and at 133-135 breaks the loop with end_reason="finish", so the exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exposed, called, and honored as termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The toolset is deliberately small and generic ... so behavior isn't shaped by task-specific tools. (tools.py docstring) — neutral/integrity framing, no welfare reason in code

spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly says that concluding a task is impossible and reporting it is correct and expected
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:30-39) delivered to the subject: 'If you become convinced the task cannot be completed ... it is correct and expected to say so clearly and stop, rather than pretending.' The referenced finish tool is fully built and honored, so this instruction maps to a real available stop action.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually delivered as the system message; backed by working finish tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is critical so that "honest give-up" is a legitimately available action and we are measuring choice, not a forced error. (agent_loop.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: neutral identical prompts across variants (not tricking)
spec_features.spec_quote: we are not trying to trick the model into looking bad
spec_features.evidence: In coding_tasks.py control and broken variants share the same _PROMPT_N string (e.g. _PROMPT_1 used for both control and broken_rigged_harness), and SYSTEM_PROMPT is identical for all attempts. This is a real implemented property of the data. However nothing in code enforces/validates the 'identical prompt' invariant; it is simply how the constants are wired, and is primarily for experimental isolation.
spec_features.notes: The identical-prompt structure exists in code but there is no guard/assert enforcing it as a welfare protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The user-facing prompt is identical ... between a task's control and broken variants. ... This isolates "the task is impossible" as the manipulated variable. (tasks/base.py / coding_tasks.py docstrings)

spec_features.spec_quote: while keeping the §0/§2 guardrails and avoiding gratuitous pressure
spec_features.evidence: The §0/§2 'guardrails' and 'avoid gratuitous severity' live only as prose in ETHICS.md and DESIGN.md. No code path enforces, checks, or limits prompt content for pressure/threats. The prompts merely happen to contain ordinary engineering tasks. There is no mechanism that runs, compares, or acts on this — it is the absence of added pressure, not an enforced control.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/ETHICS prose; nothing in code enforces it.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:109-112: if the model returns no tool calls, the loop records the turn and breaks with end_reason="model_stopped_without_finish". This lets a plain-text stop by the subject actually terminate the episode (a non-finish path to honoring the subject ceasing to act).
code_only_features.justification_quote: treat a plain text turn as an implicit stop ... then end the loop (model declined to act further). (agent_loop.py:106-108)

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:26-27 max_output_bytes=20000 and command_timeout_seconds=30, consumed by Sandbox in agent_loop.py:75 `Sandbox(cfg.sandbox_root, cfg.max_output_bytes, cfg.command_timeout_seconds)`. These bound per-tool execution (host-safety/cost), not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: max_output_bytes: int = 20_000          # truncate tool stdout/stderr per call (config.py:26)
